parts.title: Campus Conversation: Getting a Parking Permit
script: Listen to a conversation between a student and a worker at the campus parking office.
Hello. I need a parking permit for my car. Can you help me?
Sure. Are you a new student?
Yes. This is my first semester. I drive to school every day.
OK. A permit for one semester costs sixty dollars. Do you have your student ID?
Yes, here it is. Can I pay with a credit card?
Yes, you can. But you also need your car papers. Do you have them?
Oh no. I left them at home. I only brought my driver license.
That is a problem. I need the car papers to make the permit.
I live twenty minutes away. Is the office open this afternoon?
Yes. We are open until five o'clock. You can come back after your class.
Great. Also, where can I park with this permit?
You can park in the blue lots. The blue lot near the library is the biggest. But it fills up fast.
Yes. Try to arrive before nine in the morning. Then you can find a space easily.
Thank you. I will bring my car papers this afternoon.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the conversation.
That is a problem. I need the car papers to make the permit.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: Why Do We Recycle?
script: Listen to part of a lecture in an environmental science class.
Today we will talk about recycling. Recycling means we use old things to make new things. It is very good for our planet.
Let me start with paper. Paper comes from trees. When we recycle paper, we do not need to cut down as many trees. One ton of recycled paper can save about seventeen trees.
Next, let us talk about metal. Cans are often made of aluminum. Recycling an aluminum can uses much less energy than making a new can. In fact, it saves about ninety-five percent of the energy.

Now, think about plastic. Plastic bottles can take hundreds of years to break down in the ground. If we recycle them, they do not stay in the ground. We can make new things from them, like clothes and bags.
Recycling also helps people. Many cities have recycling programs. These programs give jobs to many workers.
So, why do we recycle? First, it saves trees. Second, it saves energy. Third, it keeps trash out of the ground.
Listen again to something I said earlier.
Many people think recycling is hard. But it is easy. Just put your bottles and cans in the right bin.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the lecture.
Let me start with paper. Paper comes from trees.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
questions.exp: The lecture is about why recycling is good.

questions.q: How many trees can one ton of recycled paper save?
How much energy does recycling an aluminum can save?
What can be made from recycled plastic bottles?
questions.exp: New clothes and bags can be made.

questions.q: Why does the professor say, "Let me start with paper"?
o: To change the topic to metal
To ask the students a question

questions.q: How does the professor organize the lecture?
o: He gives several reasons to recycle
He tells a story about a student
He gives a history of paper
questions.exp: He gives reasons: trees, energy, trash.
